h1: Investor Renovation Contractor in Green Bay
intro: Green Bay is a working city with a steady base of paper, food processing, health care, logistics and manufacturing jobs, and its housing reflects that history. The Fox River splits the city into an older west side of modest frame houses around Fort Howard and Seymour Park and an east side that runs from Victorian homes in the Astor neighborhood out to post-war ranches in Preble and newer homes near Baird Creek. Prices are moderate by Wisconsin standards, inventory is often tight, and buyers and renters both want houses that are warm, dry and updated. Genstone Construction manages renovations for investors, lenders and servicers in Green Bay and the surrounding Brown County communities. We coordinate vetted, licensed local contractors while our estimators and field managers run each project from our Romeoville, Illinois headquarters. Every engagement begins with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review, followed by a detailed scope, a draw schedule tied to completed work and a single field manager for the life of the job, with no upfront payment required.
housingStock:
Green Bay's housing tells the story of a river town that grew around mills and rail lines.

The west side holds much of the city's oldest working-class housing. Fort Howard, Tank Park and the streets around the Broadway District are filled with small one- and one-and-a-half-story frame houses and simple two-story homes from the late nineteenth century through the 1930s, many built for mill and rail workers. Lots are narrow, basements are often low and damp, and the houses have been modified many times by owners who did their own repairs. Expect old wiring, original plumbing mixed with newer patches, and foundations of stone, brick or early concrete block.

On the east side, the Astor neighborhood and the streets near Navarino and Whitney Park hold larger Victorian, Queen Anne, foursquare and Craftsman homes, some of them substantial. These houses can be strong flips or rentals, but they carry the costs of age: plaster walls, balloon framing, lead paint, knob-and-tube wiring and large, inefficient heating systems.

Moving east and north, Preble, the Bay Beach area and the streets around Joannes Park shift to post-war ranches, Cape Cods and split-levels from the 1940s through the 1970s. These homes are simpler to renovate but bring their own predictable issues, including asbestos in floor tile and siding, original electrical panels and aging sewer laterals.

Newer subdivisions near Baird Creek and in suburbs like Howard, Bellevue and Suamico include homes from the 1980s onward, where rehab tends to be cosmetic.

Across the city, two factors shape nearly every rehab budget: heavy clay soils that hold water against foundations, and a long, cold winter that punishes weak roofs, poor insulation and neglected plumbing. Houses that look similar from the street can carry very different budgets once those two factors are checked.

commonIssues.title: Wet basements in heavy clay soil
commonIssues.body: Much of Green Bay sits on dense clay that drains slowly, and areas near the Fox River, the East River and the bay can have high groundwater. Water collects against foundations during spring melt and heavy rains, and older stone or block walls let it in. Typical repairs include regrading, extending downspouts, adding interior drain tile and a sump, and repairing cracked or bowed walls. Getting water under control should come before any finished basement work.

commonIssues.title: Old wiring in west side and east side homes
commonIssues.body: Many older homes on both sides of the river still have knob-and-tube wiring, ungrounded circuits or undersized panels, often mixed with later additions done without permits. Insurers and lenders may balk at remaining knob-and-tube, and modern kitchens and appliances need more capacity than these systems provide. Rewiring is often one of the larger line items in a Green Bay rehab, and it is best priced during a Pre-Offer Rehab Review rather than discovered after demolition.

commonIssues.title: Freeze damage and ice dams
commonIssues.body: Green Bay winters are long and cold, and houses with poor attic insulation develop ice dams that drive water into ceilings and walls. Vacant or poorly heated homes are vulnerable to frozen and burst pipes, especially in exterior walls and crawlspaces. A good scope adds attic insulation and ventilation where needed, relocates or insulates vulnerable plumbing, and checks the heating system carefully before winter. Freeze damage is one of the most common findings in vacant Green Bay houses.

commonIssues.title: Lead paint and asbestos
commonIssues.body: The large majority of Green Bay's older housing predates 1978, so lead paint is common on windows, trim, porches and siding. Lead-safe work practices are part of most rehabs on the west side and in the Astor area. Post-war homes in Preble and on the east side often contain asbestos in floor tile, mastic, duct wrap and cement siding. Both hazards are manageable with proper planning, testing and abatement where materials will be disturbed.

commonIssues.title: Aging sewer laterals and plumbing
commonIssues.body: Older Green Bay homes commonly have clay or cast-iron sewer laterals that crack, sag or fill with tree roots, along with galvanized water lines that restrict flow. A camera inspection of the sewer line before purchase can reveal problems that would otherwise surface during the first heavy use. Replacing old supply lines and failing drains during the rehab avoids costly emergency repairs once a tenant or buyer is living in the house.

investorMarket:
Green Bay's investment market is steady rather than speculative, and different strategies fit different parts of the city.

On the west side, Fort Howard, Tank Park and Seymour Park offer some of the most affordable entry points in the metro. These neighborhoods suit buy-and-hold investors and BRRRR projects, since modest houses can be renovated to a durable rental standard and leased to working households who value proximity to downtown and employers. The houses are small, so scope control matters more than design.

On the east side, the Astor neighborhood and the areas around Whitney Park and Navarino attract owner-occupants who appreciate older homes with character, making them candidates for flips when the purchase price leaves room for systems updates. Preble and the neighborhoods north toward Bay Beach have plenty of post-war ranches and Cape Cods that work for both flips and rentals, depending on the condition and price.

Small multifamily is present throughout the older parts of the city, with up-and-down duplexes on the west side and near downtown, and newer side-by-side duplexes and small apartment buildings in the suburbs and on the edges of the city.

The surrounding suburbs, including De Pere, Ashwaubenon, Allouez and Howard, tend to have higher prices and stronger owner-occupant demand. Rehabs there are often lighter and more cosmetic, with flips competing against new construction.

Across the metro, a healthy job base and limited housing supply support both resale and rental demand.
permits:
Building permits within city limits are issued by the City of Green Bay's building inspection office, which reviews plans and inspects structural, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work. Remodels that change walls, replace roofs or windows in some cases, finish basements, add bathrooms or alter mechanical systems generally require permits. In Wisconsin, one- and two-family homes fall under the state's Uniform Dwelling Code, and a contractor pulling a permit for that work must hold the state's Dwelling Contractor certification. Electricians, plumbers and HVAC contractors are licensed through the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services.

On investor projects, a few local items matter. Older homes may carry open code orders that transfer with the property and need to be cleared through repairs and reinspection. Converting a single-family house to a duplex, or changing the number of units, can involve zoning review in addition to building permits.

Nearby communities such as De Pere, Ashwaubenon, Allouez and Howard each have their own building departments, with their own permit and inspection procedures. Genstone confirms the jurisdiction for every property and builds its permit and inspection steps into the project schedule.
climate:
Green Bay has one of the colder climates among Genstone's Midwest markets, with long winters, heavy snow and frequent subzero stretches. Deep frost heaves steps, slabs and porches that lack proper footings, and ice dams are a recurring problem on older, poorly insulated homes. Vacant houses can freeze quickly if heat fails, so winter acquisitions should be inspected for burst pipes and damaged boilers or furnaces before scopes are finalized.

Spring brings snowmelt and rain on top of heavy clay soils, which is when basements leak the most and when grading and drainage problems become obvious. Summers are mild and well suited to exterior work.

For scheduling, roofing, siding, masonry, concrete and exterior painting are best completed from late spring through early fall. Interior work can continue year-round as long as the house is heated and protected.

faqs.q: Is Green Bay a good market for rental investors?
faqs.a: Green Bay has a stable employment base and limited housing supply, which supports rental demand across the city. West side neighborhoods such as Fort Howard and Seymour Park offer lower entry prices, while east side and suburban rentals tend to command higher rents. The key is buying at a price that leaves room for necessary systems work. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps you test that before you commit to a property.

faqs.a: No. The company's one office is its Romeoville, Illinois headquarters, south of Chicago. For Green Bay projects, our estimators, field managers and billing team work from headquarters and coordinate vetted, licensed and insured local contractors in the Brown County area. Your field manager oversees the work and keeps progress, photos and milestones visible, so you can follow the project from anywhere without needing to visit the site.

faqs.q: When is the best time to renovate in Green Bay?
faqs.a: Interior renovations can happen any time of year as long as the house is heated. Exterior work, such as roofing, siding, masonry, concrete and painting, is best scheduled from late spring through early fall. If you buy in late fall or winter, plan interior work first and schedule exterior items for warmer months. We build those seasonal realities into every schedule and draw plan.

faqs.q: Do you work in the suburbs around Green Bay?
faqs.a: Yes. We work across Brown County, including De Pere, Ashwaubenon, Allouez, Howard, Bellevue and Suamico. Each community has its own building department and permit process, and housing styles vary, from older homes in parts of De Pere to newer subdivisions in Howard and Suamico. Our scopes reflect the jurisdiction and the type of house involved, so a suburban project is not priced like a west side rehab.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Fix and flip renovations in Green Bay scoped for east side, west side and Preble buyers. Free pre-offer rehab review, finish plans and draws tied to work.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Green Bay
fix-flip.intro: Green Bay buyers are practical. They want a house that is warm in January, dry in April and updated enough that they will not be replacing the furnace or the roof in their first few years. Flips that deliver on those basics, with clean, current finishes that match the neighborhood, tend to sell well in a market where good inventory is often limited. Flips that put money into flashy kitchens while leaving a wet basement or old wiring behind tend to struggle at inspection. Genstone Construction scopes Green Bay flips around that reality. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates repair costs, refines your after-repair value against recent local sales and tells you whether the deal supports your offer. You then receive a detailed scope with finish options and a draw schedule, and one field manager runs the job until it is ready to list.

sections.h2: Choosing the right Green Bay flip
sections.body: The best Green Bay flips usually fall into two groups. The first is the post-war ranch or Cape Cod in Preble, near Joannes Park or toward Bay Beach that has good bones but dated finishes, old mechanicals and perhaps a damp basement. These houses appeal to first-time buyers and downsizers, and a well-executed update can bring them in line with recently renovated comps. The second group is the older east side house in the Astor or Whitney Park area, where buyers appreciate original woodwork, larger rooms and front porches but expect modern systems. Those projects carry higher costs and more unknowns, so they require a careful scope. West side houses in Fort Howard and Seymour Park can work as flips when the purchase price is low, though many investors find them better suited to rentals. Our estimators help you sort these options based on real repair costs and realistic resale values before you make an offer. That keeps you from committing to a house whose numbers only work in a best-case scenario.

sections.h2: What Green Bay buyers and inspectors look for
sections.body: Most Green Bay buyers hire a home inspector, and the reports on older houses tend to focus on the same concerns. Water in the basement or signs of past water damage are near the top, followed by outdated or unsafe wiring, old furnaces or boilers, aging roofs, galvanized plumbing and inadequate attic insulation. On mid-century homes, asbestos tile and original electrical panels often appear in reports. Addressing these items in the scope protects your sale price. We include drainage and foundation repairs where needed, update electrical and plumbing under permits from the City of Green Bay, replace aging heating equipment and add insulation to cut ice dam risk. Lead-safe practices are followed on older painted surfaces. When it is time to list, you have a record of permits, replaced systems and progress photos, which can reassure buyers and lenders. In a practical market like this one, that documentation can matter as much as the finishes buyers see during a showing.

sections.h2: Scheduling a Green Bay flip around winter
sections.body: Green Bay's winters shape every flip schedule. A house purchased in fall should have its exterior needs addressed first, including roofing, siding, gutters, windows and any foundation or drainage repairs, before snow and deep cold make that work difficult. If that is not possible, exterior items can be planned for spring, but the house must be weathertight and heated through the winter. Interior work, such as kitchens, baths, flooring, drywall and paint, continues steadily through the cold months. Many investors aim to finish interior work during winter and list in spring, when buyer activity typically increases. We build those realities into the scope and the draw schedule, separating exterior and interior phases so weather affects only the parts of the job it should. Your field manager reports progress against milestones so you know whether the project is on pace for your target listing date. If problems arise, such as hidden water damage, you hear about them right away.

faqs.q: What finish level should I choose for a Green Bay flip?
faqs.a: It depends on the neighborhood and recent sales. In Preble and similar areas, clean, durable finishes with updated kitchens and baths usually match the comps. In the Astor area, buyers may pay more for preserved woodwork and higher-quality finishes. Our estimates often include more than one finish plan so you can compare costs against likely resale value before you commit to a direction.

faqs.q: Can Genstone help with flip financing in Green Bay?
faqs.a: Within the Genstone Companies, Genstone Financial lends on flips and also writes lines of credit, DSCR rental loans and new construction loans. Some investors use Genstone Financial alongside our renovation services, while others work with their own lender. In both cases, our detailed scope and draw schedule give the lender clear information about the work and how funds will be released at each stage.

faqs.q: Do I pay anything before work begins on my flip?
faqs.a: No. Nothing is due to Genstone before the work starts. Construction draws are tied to completed work that your field manager documents with photos and notes, and final payment comes after completion and your approval. Dumpster and debris costs are included in the estimate, which matters on older Green Bay homes where demolition of plaster, old flooring and basement clutter can generate a lot of material.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR renovations in Green Bay built for the refinance appraisal and long-term rental durability, from west side cottages to east side post-war ranches.
brrrr.intro: Green Bay offers a combination that BRRRR investors look for: affordable older houses, a stable workforce that rents, and enough recently updated sales to support a refinance appraisal. The challenge is that many of the cheapest houses, particularly on the west side, need more than paint and flooring. Wet basements, old wiring, tired furnaces and poor insulation are common, and if they are not handled during the rehab, they become the repair calls that erode rental income. Genstone Construction scopes Green Bay BRRRR projects to meet both goals at once: a property that appraises as fully updated and a rental that holds up through years of tenants and winters. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates repairs and refines your after-repair value before you buy, and our draw schedule follows how rehab lenders release funds.

sections.h2: Finding the spread in Green Bay
sections.body: BRRRR returns depend on the spread between what you put into a property and what it appraises for afterward. In Green Bay, that spread most often appears on houses that look dated rather than distressed. Examples include a west side story-and-a-half in Fort Howard with original kitchen and bath but a solid structure, a ranch in Preble with old carpet over hardwood and an aging furnace, or an estate sale near Joannes Park that has been well cared for but not updated in decades. These houses can be bought below the price of renovated comps and brought up to their level without structural surprises. Houses with major foundation movement or extensive water damage can still work, but the margin is thinner, and the appraisal rarely credits the full cost of structural repair. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review evaluates these factors and gives you a realistic cost and value range before you commit. That helps you bid confidently on the right houses and walk away from the wrong ones without regret.

sections.h2: Renovating to the Green Bay appraisal
sections.body: Appraisers in Green Bay compare your property with recent sales of similar houses nearby. To earn the strongest refinance value, the rehab should place the house clearly among the updated comps. That typically means a functional, modern kitchen, a renovated bathroom, new or refinished flooring, fresh paint, updated lighting, and documented upgrades to heating, electrical and plumbing. A dry basement matters as well, because water stains and musty odors raise questions for appraisers and lenders. Where comps show finished lower levels, adding living space may help, but only if the basement can be kept dry and meets egress requirements for any bedroom. We pull permits from the City of Green Bay or the appropriate suburb and keep records that support the appraisal. Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans for investors who want to keep the refinance within the same group, though you are free to use any lender you choose.

sections.h2: Durability for a long Green Bay hold
sections.body: A BRRRR property is meant to be held, so durability matters as much as appraisal value. In Green Bay, durability starts with water and heat. Grading, gutters, downspout extensions and, where needed, interior drainage and a sump pump keep basements dry through spring melt. Attic insulation and air sealing reduce ice dams and heating costs, making the property more attractive to tenants who pay their own utilities. A new, efficient furnace or boiler installed during the rehab avoids emergency replacements during subzero weather. Inside, durable flooring such as luxury vinyl plank stands up to boots, salt and snow tracked in all winter. Simple, widely available fixtures make future repairs easy. Lead-safe work on older painted surfaces protects families with young children. Our one-year workmanship warranty covers the work we install, while tenant damage and normal wear fall outside it, so choosing tough materials during the rehab keeps long-term costs down.

faqs.q: Which Green Bay neighborhoods suit BRRRR?
faqs.a: West side neighborhoods such as Fort Howard, Tank Park and Seymour Park offer lower purchase prices and steady rental demand, while east side areas like Preble provide post-war houses that renovate predictably. The right choice depends on the specific property and comps. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps you compare the numbers for each candidate before you make an offer on any of them.

faqs.q: How do you document a BRRRR rehab for the refinance?
faqs.a: Your field manager records each stage of work with photos, notes and milestones, and we keep permits and inspection records on file. At the end of the project, you have a clear summary of updated systems and finishes. That documentation helps appraisers understand the scope of the renovation and supports your refinance lender's review of the property and its condition.

faqs.q: Should I add a bedroom in the basement?
faqs.a: Only if the basement can be kept dry, has adequate ceiling height and can include a code-compliant egress window. In Green Bay's clay soils, water management must come first. If comparable updated homes nearby have finished lower levels and extra bedrooms, the addition may raise the appraisal. If not, the money may be better spent on kitchens, baths and systems.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family and duplex rental renovations in Green Bay built for cold winters, wet basements and tenant turnover, with consistent portfolio specifications.
rental-renovation.h1: Rental Property Renovations in Green Bay
rental-renovation.intro: Green Bay renters are often working households employed in health care, manufacturing, logistics and food processing, and they tend to stay longer in homes that are comfortable and affordable to heat. For landlords, that means durable, efficient rentals can produce steady income with fewer turnovers, while houses that leak, freeze or burn through heating dollars cycle tenants and generate repair calls. Genstone Construction renovates Green Bay single-family rentals and duplexes to a consistent standard built for local conditions. We write portfolio specifications for finishes and systems, plan work around vacancies and seasons, and assign a field manager who coordinates vetted local contractors and keeps documentation visible to you and your property manager. Genstone Property Management and Genstone Field Services are also part of the Genstone Companies for owners who want continuing support after the renovation.

sections.h2: A rental standard built for Green Bay winters
sections.body: Rentals in Green Bay face months of snow, salt, subzero cold and spring meltwater, and the specification should reflect that. Flooring near entries and in kitchens and baths should resist water and salt; luxury vinyl plank and tile perform well. Entry doors and storm doors need tight weatherstripping. Attic insulation and air sealing reduce ice dams and lower heating bills for tenants, which helps retention. Furnaces and water heaters should be in good condition before a new lease begins, since failures in midwinter are both costly and disruptive. In older homes on the west side and in the Astor area, the standard should also include safe, updated electrical, replaced galvanized supply lines where present and lead-safe surfaces. We write these requirements into a single specification so every property in your portfolio is renovated to the same baseline, making maintenance and future turns more predictable. Our estimators then price each new acquisition against that baseline, which speeds decisions.

sections.h2: Keeping Green Bay basements dry and usable
sections.body: Basement water is one of the most common rental complaints in Green Bay, and it is closely tied to the area's heavy clay soils and spring snowmelt. Tenants rely on basements for laundry and storage, and recurring water leads to damaged belongings, mold concerns and turnover. Solving the problem during a renovation is far less expensive than responding to repeated complaints. Typical steps include regrading soil away from the foundation, cleaning and extending gutters and downspouts, sealing cracks, and installing interior drain tile with a sump pump where needed. Bowed or cracked walls may need bracing or repair. Once water is controlled, basements can be cleaned, painted and fitted with sturdy laundry hookups. We document the work and condition of each basement so you and your property manager can track it over time. In older west side homes with low stone foundations, managing expectations is important; the goal is dry, usable space rather than finished living area.

Not every rental needs a full renovation between tenants. Many Green Bay units need a quick turn: paint, flooring repairs, appliance checks, cleaning and repair of any damage. Genstone Field Services handles turn and make-ready work, inspections, occupied maintenance and code compliance, so the same organization that renovated the property can keep it ready to lease. When a turn reveals larger issues, such as a failing furnace, an aging roof or a sewer lateral that has started backing up, your field manager can scope and price a project with its own draw schedule. Seasonal planning matters as well. Units that become vacant in winter are good candidates for interior updates, while roofing, siding and exterior paint found during a winter turn are scheduled for warmer months. Our one-year workmanship warranty covers the work we install, but not tenant damage or normal wear and tear, which is why durable choices pay off.

faqs.q: Can you renovate occupied rentals in Green Bay?
faqs.a: Yes, depending on the scope. Many projects, such as furnace or water heater replacement, electrical updates and exterior work, can be completed with tenants in place if access and scheduling are planned carefully. Larger interior renovations are usually easier when the unit is vacant. Your field manager coordinates schedules with you or your property manager and keeps work areas safe for residents.

faqs.q: Do you work on rental portfolios with several properties?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone works with individual investors, funds and institutional owners, and our network of licensed local contractors allows us to manage multiple properties in the Green Bay area. Each property receives its own scope, estimate and draw schedule, while a shared specification keeps materials and finishes consistent across your portfolio. You can follow progress on every property without visiting each address in person.

faqs.q: What does Genstone's warranty cover on rentals?
faqs.a: Genstone offers a one-year workmanship warranty on the work we perform. Tenant-caused damage and the everyday wear of an occupied home fall outside it. If an item we installed fails because of how it was installed, we will address it. Selecting durable, rental-grade materials during the renovation helps reduce the wear-related repairs that fall outside any warranty, particularly entry flooring exposed to winter salt.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2–4 Unit Renovation in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Renovations for Green Bay up-and-down duplexes, side-by-side duplexes and small 2–4 unit buildings, with phased work in occupied units and shared systems.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Duplex and 2–4 Unit Renovations in Green Bay
multifamily-renovation.intro: Small multifamily properties in Green Bay come in a few familiar shapes. Older up-and-down duplexes sit on the west side and around downtown, often in houses that were built as two units or divided decades ago. Side-by-side duplexes from the 1960s and 1970s appear on the edges of the city and in suburbs, and small apartment buildings of three or four units are scattered through older neighborhoods and along commercial corridors. Each type has different renovation needs, but all share the challenges of shared systems, fire separation and tenants who may still be living in the building. Genstone Construction renovates Green Bay duplexes and 2–4 unit properties for investors, phasing work around occupied units and pricing shared systems separately. Every project starts with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review and a detailed scope.

sections.body: On Green Bay's west side and near downtown, many two-unit buildings stack one apartment above another, sometimes with a shared entry and stairway and sometimes with separate doors. These buildings are typically older, with plaster walls, older wiring, galvanized and cast-iron plumbing, and foundations of stone or block. A renovation scope usually covers two kitchens and two baths, but the more important work is often structural and mechanical: safe stairways and porches, updated electrical service sized for two households, plumbing stacks that serve both units, and fire separation between floors. Where heating is shared, separating systems can make tenant billing simpler and improve net income, though it adds cost. Lead-safe practices apply to most of these buildings, and basement water management protects shared laundry and storage areas. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices each unit and the shared systems separately, so you can see where the money goes and how the building compares to your expected rents. That breakdown also helps when you approach a lender for financing.

sections.h2: Side-by-side duplexes and small apartment buildings
sections.body: Side-by-side duplexes built in the 1960s and 1970s are common on the outer edges of Green Bay and in nearby suburbs. They often have separate utilities and mirrored layouts, which simplifies renovation. Typical needs include dated kitchens and baths, original windows, worn flooring, older furnaces and water heaters, and sometimes asbestos in floor tile or siding. The shared roof and party wall should be inspected carefully, especially when one side has been maintained better than the other. Small three- and four-unit buildings add common hallways, shared laundry and sometimes a single boiler or water heater serving all units. Fire separation, common-area lighting, smoke and carbon monoxide detection, and secure entry doors deserve attention. We generally renovate all units to the same specification so rents, appraisals and maintenance stay consistent. Exterior work such as roofing and siding is scheduled as one project for the entire building during warmer months, which avoids paying for two mobilizations and keeps the building's appearance uniform.

sections.h2: Phasing work around Green Bay tenants
sections.body: Many small multifamily buildings in Green Bay are purchased with at least one unit occupied, and keeping that income during the renovation is usually a priority. Phasing allows the building to improve without displacing tenants. A typical plan renovates vacant units first, then schedules shared-system work such as electrical service upgrades, heating changes, roofing and basement waterproofing with advance notice and planned shutoffs. Occupied units are renovated when tenants move out. In Green Bay's climate, timing is especially important: heating changes should be completed before cold weather arrives, and any interruption to heat in winter must be brief and planned. Lead-safe containment protects occupied units in older buildings, and common areas are cleaned and kept safe at the end of each workday. Your field manager coordinates access with tenants and your property manager and posts updates so you can track progress on each unit and the building as a whole.

faqs.q: Should I separate utilities in a Green Bay duplex?
faqs.a: Separating heat and electric can lower your operating costs and make the building easier to manage, but it requires new equipment, gas piping and electrical work. Many side-by-side duplexes already have separate utilities, while older up-and-down duplexes often do not. We price separation as its own line item so you can compare the cost with your expected hold period and rents.

faqs.q: Can tenants stay in a Green Bay duplex while you work?
faqs.a: Yes. We usually renovate the vacant unit first, schedule shared-system work with notice and short interruptions, and renovate the occupied unit when it turns over. Your field manager plans access and safety measures, especially in older buildings where lead-safe containment is important, and keeps you updated throughout the project. Heating work is timed before cold weather so the occupied side is never left without heat for long.

faqs.q: Will Genstone take on a Green Bay triplex or fourplex?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone renovates properties with two to four units. In Green Bay, these include older converted houses, purpose-built small apartment buildings and suburban multifamily properties. Each project gets a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review, a detailed scope that separates units and shared systems, and a draw schedule tied to completed work. Common hallways, shared laundry and fire separation are priced as their own items so you can see their cost clearly.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor in Green Bay for buyers, agents and lenders: bids, consultant coordination and draws for older and post-war homes.
fha-203k.intro: For many Green Bay buyers, the FHA 203(k) loan turns an overlooked house into a realistic first home. A west side story-and-a-half with an old furnace and a damp basement, an Astor area Victorian with outdated wiring, or a Preble ranch with original kitchen and asbestos tile might not pass a standard FHA appraisal, but with a 203(k), the buyer can finance both the purchase and the repairs in one mortgage. Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, and we work with Green Bay buyers, real estate agents and loan officers to prepare the bids, scope documents and draw schedules the program requires. Our aim is to keep the renovation side organized so closings stay on track, and to deliver the completed work the loan was designed to fund.

sections.h2: Standard versus Limited 203(k) in Green Bay
sections.body: Genstone uses the FHA 203(k) thresholds as stated on our site: the minimum repair amount is $5,000, a HUD consultant inspection becomes part of the process above $15,000, and the Limited 203(k) caps repairs at $75,000 and does not permit structural work. In Green Bay, a Limited 203(k) often fits a post-war ranch or Cape Cod needing a new furnace, updated electrical, new windows, flooring and a kitchen refresh. A Standard 203(k) is better suited to houses that need foundation repair, structural changes, major water management or extensive work on an older west side or east side home. Choosing correctly at the beginning matters because changing programs mid-process can delay closing. Our estimators look for warning signs such as bowed basement walls, sagging floors and water damage early, so buyers and loan officers can make an informed decision before the appraisal and underwriting move forward. West side houses with stone foundations deserve extra scrutiny here.

sections.h2: Typical 203(k) work on Green Bay houses
sections.body: Many Green Bay 203(k) projects share a pattern of required health and safety work combined with improvements the buyer wants. Required items commonly include peeling paint on pre-1978 houses, which calls for lead-safe work, outdated or unsafe wiring, failing roofs, aging heating systems, missing handrails, and moisture problems in basements caused by clay soils and spring melt. Freeze damage to plumbing is another frequent finding in houses that were vacant over winter. Optional improvements often include kitchen and bath updates, refinished or new flooring, and energy upgrades such as attic insulation and new windows, which make a real difference in heating costs here. We separate required and optional items in the bid so the buyer and lender can see what must be completed and what can be adjusted if the appraisal or budget is tight. That approach helps buyers make informed decisions without risking the loan approval or the closing date.

sections.h2: Working with consultants, lenders and draws
sections.body: On a Standard 203(k), a HUD consultant prepares the work write-up, and our bid must match it line by line. We review the consultant's report, flag items that may cost more once walls or floors are opened in an older Green Bay house, and keep revisions to a minimum so the lender is not left waiting. After closing, our field manager obtains the permits the work requires from the City of Green Bay or the relevant suburb and schedules inspections. Money for the renovation comes out of the lender's escrow in stages, each one released after an inspector confirms the work and our field manager submits the photo record. Seasonal timing matters: if closing happens in late fall, exterior items such as roofing or siding may need to be scheduled for spring, and we coordinate that plan with the lender. Buyers have a single point of contact who explains progress and next steps, which makes the process far less stressful.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) loan be used on a Green Bay duplex?
faqs.a: Yes. FHA permits 203(k) financing on properties with one to four units when the borrower lives in one unit as a primary residence. That makes the program useful for buyers interested in Green Bay's older up-and-down duplexes. Your loan officer confirms eligibility, and we can prepare a bid covering each unit and shared systems such as heating and the roof.

faqs.q: How does a buyer request a 203(k) bid from Genstone?
faqs.a: Send us the property address, listing information and, if available, the consultant's work write-up or inspection report. Our estimators review the house and prepare a scope and bid in the format the lender requires. If the consultant has not yet visited, we can provide a preliminary estimate to help the buyer and agent decide whether the property is a good fit.

faqs.q: Is any payment due to Genstone before 203(k) work starts?
faqs.a: No. In a 203(k) loan, renovation funds are held by the lender and released in stages after completed work is inspected. Genstone does not require upfront payment, and final payment follows completion and approval. Our field manager coordinates draw inspections and provides the photos and documentation the lender needs to release each payment. Buyers never have to front construction money themselves.

reo-renovation.title: REO Property Renovation in Green Bay, WI | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO and bank-owned renovations in Green Bay for servicers, banks, GSEs and investors: freeze damage, wet basements, mold, code orders and resale repairs.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Renovations in Green Bay
reo-renovation.intro: Vacant and bank-owned houses in Green Bay face a harsh test every winter. When heat is shut off or a furnace fails, pipes freeze and burst, water pours into ceilings and basements, and by spring the house may have mold, warped floors and damaged mechanicals. Add heavy clay soils that push water into older foundations, and an REO property can deteriorate quickly if no one is watching it. Genstone Construction works with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and investors buying REO in Green Bay and Brown County, and we are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Together with Genstone Field Services, we can secure, inspect, document and repair a vacant property and bring it back to a condition that supports a sale.

sections.body: The most common problem in vacant Green Bay houses is damage from cold and water. Supply lines in exterior walls and crawlspaces split when heat is lost, boilers and radiators crack, and toilets and traps break. When temperatures rise, water from those failures runs into floors, walls and basements, saturating plaster, drywall, insulation and wood. Meanwhile, spring melt and rain can push groundwater through cracked or porous foundations. We begin by documenting conditions thoroughly with photos and notes, pressure-testing the plumbing, checking the heating system and looking for moisture throughout the house. Our scope separates urgent work, such as winterization, water removal, mold remediation and securing the structure, from repairs needed to make the property marketable. Asset managers can approve emergency items quickly while evaluating the larger scope with complete information. That sequencing limits further deterioration and keeps repair costs from growing while decisions are pending. It also provides a clear record for insurance and investor reporting.

A vacant property in Green Bay requires continuous attention. Snow must be removed from walks, roofs should be checked for ice dams and damage, and heating or winterization must be verified regularly. In warmer months, lawns grow, debris accumulates and open or broken windows invite trespassing. Neglected properties can receive code orders from the city, which then need to be resolved before or during a sale. Genstone Field Services handles property preservation, including lawn care, snow removal, debris removal, lock changes and periodic inspections, as well as code compliance work. When orders exist, we review them, price the necessary repairs, obtain permits from the City of Green Bay or the appropriate suburb, and arrange reinspection. Keeping the property secure and compliant protects its value and supports a smoother sale. Regular inspection reports with photos give asset managers a current picture of the property even when they cannot visit it themselves.

sections.h2: Preparing Green Bay REO for market
sections.body: Once a property is stabilized, the next decision is how much repair work will produce the best outcome. Some Green Bay REO homes only need to reach a condition acceptable to FHA or conventional lenders: working heat, safe electrical, sound plumbing, a functioning kitchen and bath, a roof without active leaks and a basement free of standing water. Others, especially well-located ranches in Preble or older homes in the Astor area, may justify fuller renovations because owner-occupant buyers will pay for move-in condition. West side properties in Fort Howard or Seymour Park may sell best to investors at a stabilized, rent-ready level. For Brown County assets we often write two or three repair levels side by side, each fully priced, so the asset manager can pick the one that fits the street. Throughout the project, we provide documentation, permits, lien waivers and milestone updates, with a single field manager responsible from first visit to completion. Listing in spring, when buyer activity usually picks up, is often worth planning around.

faqs.q: Who does Genstone work with on Green Bay REO?
faqs.a: We work with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and individual investors buying bank-owned properties, and we are a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. Each client receives a detailed scope, photo documentation and a field manager who stays with the property from start to finish, along with preservation support from Genstone Field Services when needed. Scopes can be prepared at more than one repair level.

faqs.q: How do you handle mold in a vacant Green Bay house?
faqs.a: We document affected areas, identify and correct the moisture source, remove damaged materials and include remediation as a defined scope item. In Green Bay, mold often follows frozen pipes, roof leaks or basement water from clay soils and snowmelt. Fixing the cause is part of the plan so the problem does not return after the property is sold or occupied.

faqs.q: Can you clear code violations on a Green Bay property?
faqs.a: Yes. We review outstanding orders, price the repairs needed to resolve them, obtain any required permits and coordinate reinspection. Genstone Field Services also provides ongoing preservation and code compliance services, which help prevent new violations while the property is vacant and awaiting a decision on repairs or sale. You receive documentation showing each order resolved, which is useful for the closing file and for buyers who ask about the property's history.
